meta.title: OBD-II / DTC reference
meta.note: Curated common + Ford/EcoBoost-specific codes with diagnostic guidance. Any code not listed still resolves to its category via range fallback. Not a substitute for a factory service procedure — verify against the applicable manual and confirm on the actual vehicle.
meta.sources: SAE J2012 generic definitions + Focus ST knowledge base (docs/knowledge-base/05 Diagnostics & DTC).

ranges.hint: Sensors, fuel trim, O2/lambda, MAF/MAP, injector circuits.
Mass air/volume, IAT/ECT, throttle/pedal, injector circuits.
Misfire detection, knock sensor, crank/cam correlation.
EGR, EVAP/purge, catalyst, secondary air, crankcase vent.
VSS, idle control, brake/clutch switch, cruise.
PCM/ECM internal, processor, module outputs, torque.
Ford-specific engine/trans code — check Ford definition.
ABS, traction/stability, steering, suspension, wheel speed.
CAN bus, lost communication, module/config faults.

codes.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger 'A' Underboost
codes.desc: Actual boost is below what the PCM commanded.
causes: Loose/split charge pipe or intercooler coupler
codes.guidance: Divide the problem: is the PCM commanding more boost than the engine makes, and is boost actually low or a sensor artifact? Confirm the tune/map + target, then inspect every charge connection (especially any that separated before), intercooler core/end-tanks + pipe O-rings, run a controlled smoke/pressure test, check the bypass valve + boost-control solenoid hoses/electrical, verify wastegate linkage/preload per procedure. Common error: buying a turbo before finding a loose charge pipe.

codes.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Overboost Condition
codes.guidance: Stop aggressive driving. Verify the correct map (no tune mismatch), inspect boost-control plumbing for crossed/split/pinched/disconnected hoses, verify MAP/TMAP plausibility key-on and under load, inspect the wastegate for binding/improper preload, and compare commanded vs actual boost + wastegate duty. Return to a known-safe calibration. Overboost is not free power.

codes.title: Crankcase Ventilation System Disconnected
codes.desc: PCV/crankcase-vent flow or integrity outside expected range.
causes: Catch-can/PCV modification not matched to calibration
Vacuum leak in the crankcase-vent path
codes.guidance: Treat it as a case, not a parts order. Inspect crankcase-vent plumbing, connection integrity, routing, restrictions and modifications; confirm the current calibration expects the installed PCV architecture; smoke/pressure-test appropriately; record fuel trims and crankcase behavior. Correct physical faults before calibration work. A permanent DTC can remain after a good repair until the monitor completes enough qualifying cycles.

codes.title: Unable to Bleed Up Fuel Tank Vacuum
codes.desc: Excessive fuel-tank vacuum the system can't relieve — often a stuck-open purge valve.
codes.guidance: High priority on this platform. Record fuel level + whether the symptom followed refueling; ask about rough idle/stall after fill, hard filling, tank deformation. Verify the purge-valve campaign (e.g. 18S32/26S40) + PCM calibration status by VIN first. Observe purge command + fuel trims at idle, test purge-valve sealing/flow per Ford, inspect hoses/canister/vapor lines, confirm monitor completion — don't just clear the MIL.

codes.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (very small)
codes.guidance: Check the capless filler sealing first, then hoses, purge sealing, and the canister. Smoke-test at the correct low pressure. Confirm the leak monitor completes rather than only clearing the code.

codes.title: EVAP Canister Purge Vapor Line Restriction/Flow
codes.desc: Purge-vapor line restriction or flow fault.
codes.guidance: Inspect the purge valve, plumbing, and the current applicable bulletin. Verify flow per Ford rather than guessing at the valve.

codes.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
codes.desc: Downstream O2 response suggests the catalyst isn't converting efficiently — or the data is being contaminated.
causes: Exhaust leak near the rear O2 sensor
codes.guidance: Distinguish real degradation from contaminated data: inspect for accompanying misfire/fuel-trim/purge/O2 codes, identify the downpipe + cat hardware, inspect exhaust leaks + sensor install/wiring, and analyze upstream vs downstream sensor behavior at temperature. Correct engine-control faults before condemning the cat, and verify emissions legality before changing hardware/calibration.

codes.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.guidance: Check purge early (especially post-refuel). Save trims + freeze frame, test purge-valve sealing/command, check injector leakage + rail-pressure behavior, inspect O2 wiring + exhaust leaks, confirm fuel blend/map, and verify the sensor with controlled data before replacing it.

codes.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure Too Low
codes.desc: Actual fuel-rail pressure fell below commanded.
codes.guidance: Gather low-side pressure, commanded vs actual high-pressure rail, sensor plausibility, fuel composition/temp, and load/RPM at divergence. Confirm blend + no contamination, verify battery/charging + sensor wiring, test low-side delivery, then commanded vs actual rail pressure under controlled operation. Don't keep high-load logging when actual rail pressure falls materially below commanded.

codes.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
codes.guidance: Verify sensor plausibility against commanded pressure and known-good data before replacing the sensor; rule out a real pressure-control fault first.

codes.title: MAP/BARO Sensor Range/Performance
codes.guidance: Check MAP/TMAP data key-on and under load, look for vacuum/charge leaks and intake changes, and confirm the calibration matches the installed hardware.

codes.title: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire
codes.guidance: Save freeze frame + cylinder counters, confirm correct fuel + map, inspect all plugs by cylinder, check charge-air/vacuum integrity + fuel trims, and compare commanded vs actual rail pressure. Multiple cylinders at high load with a rail-pressure drop points to fuel supply/calibration — not all four coils. Don't WOT with a flashing MIL.

codes.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire
codes.guidance: Swap-test the coil (save counters first) to see if the fault follows; inspect the plug, boot and well; check injector operation; run compression/leakdown if mechanical condition is uncertain.

codes.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire
codes.guidance: Same approach as P0301, on cylinder 2.

codes.title: Cylinder 3 Misfire
codes.guidance: Same approach as P0301, on cylinder 3.

codes.title: Cylinder 4 Misfire
codes.guidance: Same approach as P0301, on cylinder 4.

codes.title: 'A' Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
codes.desc: Intake cam timing more advanced than commanded.
codes.guidance: Check oil level/condition and the oil-control (VCT) solenoid first; low or dirty oil is a common cause. Inspect the phaser and chain if the solenoid is good.

codes.title: Crankshaft/Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
codes.desc: Crank and cam signals don't correlate.
codes.guidance: Verify mechanical timing (chain/phaser) before replacing sensors; confirm oil-control valve function.

codes.title: Coolant Thermostat (Below Regulating Temp)
codes.desc: Engine not reaching expected temperature in time.
codes.guidance: Usually a thermostat stuck open; verify coolant level and ECT accuracy before replacing.

codes.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
codes.desc: Long-term fuel trim indicates a persistent lean condition.
causes: Unmetered air / vacuum or charge leak
codes.guidance: Find unmetered air (smoke test), check MAF reading and fuel pressure. On a boosted engine, inspect charge-air integrity.

codes.title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
codes.desc: Lean condition on bank 2 (N/A on an inline-4).
codes.guidance: Same as P0171; bank 2 applies to V-engines.

codes.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
codes.guidance: Check fuel pressure, injector leakage, MAF, and purge sealing.

codes.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response (B1S1)
codes.guidance: Inspect wiring, exhaust leaks, power/ground/heater; verify with data before replacement. Downpipe/tune changes affect this.

codes.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (B1S1)
codes.guidance: Test heater power/ground and element resistance; check the fuse and connector.

codes.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
codes.guidance: Same approach as P0420, bank 2.

codes.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (small)
codes.guidance: Smoke-test; check filler sealing and hoses first.

codes.title: EVAP System Leak Detected (large/gross)
codes.guidance: Check the filler seal and obvious disconnected/loose plumbing first.

codes.title: EGR Flow Insufficient
codes.guidance: Inspect/clean EGR passages and valve; verify the flow sensor.

codes.title: Knock Sensor 1 Circuit
codes.guidance: Check sensor torque, wiring and connector; a false open reduces knock protection.

codes.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
codes.desc: Crank sensor signal fault — can cause stall/no-start.
codes.guidance: Verify sensor signal and reluctor condition; a dropout causes stalling.

codes.title: Camshaft Position Sensor 'A' Circuit
codes.guidance: Check sensor and wiring; rule out timing (P0016 family) if correlation is affected.

codes.title: Idle Air Control System
codes.guidance: Clean the throttle body and check for vacuum leaks; relearn idle.

codes.title: System Voltage Low
codes.guidance: Test battery + charging and clean grounds; low voltage creates unrelated module/comm faults.

codes.title: PCM/ECM Processor Fault
codes.guidance: Verify power/grounds and calibration integrity before condemning the module.

codes.title: Internal Control Module Torque Performance
codes.guidance: Check MAP/TMAP/throttle data, vacuum/charge leaks, and whether intake changes need calibration.

codes.title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
codes.guidance: Look for unmetered air (charge leak), verify MAP/MAF/throttle data, and confirm calibration matches the hardware.

codes.title: Lost Communication With ECM/PCM
codes.desc: A module lost communication with the PCM.
codes.guidance: Save a full topology scan, check battery resting/cranking/charging, and inspect recent work first. Identify which module actually stopped talking vs which merely reports losing it — don't replace a module because others report losing communication with it.

codes.title: Lost Communication With ABS Module
codes.desc: Lost communication with the ABS/traction module.
codes.guidance: Check ABS module power/ground and CAN continuity; scan all modules.

codes.title: Lost Communication With Body Control Module
codes.guidance: Inspect recent electrical/config work; verify BCM power/ground and network.

codes.title: Lost Communication With Instrument Panel Cluster
codes.guidance: Check cluster power/ground and CAN; revert any recent FORScan as-built change on the IPC.

codes.title: Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
codes.desc: The transmission controller requested the MIL — a companion code holds the detail.
codes.guidance: Read the accompanying transmission code; P0700 itself only points at the trans subsystem.

codes.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit
codes.guidance: Verify sensor signal and wiring.

codes.title: Left Front Wheel Speed Sensor Circuit
codes.guidance: Inspect the sensor, tone ring and wiring; compare all four wheel-speed signals.

codes.title: ECU Is Defective
codes.desc: A body-domain module reports an internal fault.
codes.guidance: Verify power/grounds and check for water intrusion before replacing the module.
